success_patterns: Each time the agent picked the hub: the plain option that states the stem's own claim with the stem's own objects, ranges and quantifier order. Every competitor was a one-edit variant of it.

Unconditional riders were rejected. These were a uniform-in-T clause, a list of constants the bounds depend on, 'every weak solution automatically satisfies...', and an extra continuity-in-H^1 clause. A rider was accepted only if the stem hypotheses derive it, and none were derivable here.
Truncations were rejected. An existence-only option lost to existence plus uniqueness, and a one-way 'if' option lost to the 'precisely if' characterization the stem asked for.

Quantifier and range swaps were rejected: 'every r' for 'a.e. r', 'every f' for 'generic f', strict '<' or one-sided '≥' for '=', limsup replaced by liminf, and u_x replaced by ||u_x||_{L^2}. Each swap was checked against the natural blow-up quantity or the generic/a.e. structure of the result.

Changed or dropped hypotheses were rejected. Examples: dropping p≥5, swapping the supercuspidal prime p for some other prime ℓ, and weakening supercuspidal to discrete series. The correct option used every stem hypothesis exactly as stated.
The agent compared option pairs on the single differing clause. It never judged options by overall look or length.

patch.reasoning: All four successes follow rules the skill already has: hub test, rider rejection, truncation rejection, and the iff and quantifier checks. The rejected previous edit (a new Step 0 plus deleted sections) lowered the score, so I will not restructure or delete anything. I add one short, trigger-based line that makes the winning procedure explicit. It names the hub as the option sharing the stem's vocabulary, states which differing clause types to reject, and gives the one test that separates a legitimate upgrade from a rider. It is brief and does not touch the protected workflow or the slow-update block.

edits.target: 10. Strength ladder (use when options are nested variants, and always for 'strongest / exact / complete' stems)
edits.content: 11. Verbatim-hub check (quick form of steps 8-10, which stays binding). Find the option that reuses the stem's own objects, hypotheses and quantifier order with nothing added or dropped, and call it S. Then classify every other option by its one differing clause. (a) The clause deletes or swaps a stem hypothesis, prime, range or quantifier, or turns limsup into liminf or 'a.e./generic' into 'every': reject. (b) The clause adds an unconditional dependence list, uniformity, 'automatically', 'unique' or an extra regularity or continuity property that the stem's hypotheses do not give in 2-3 lines: reject. (c) The clause removes a part of S (uniqueness, the converse direction, the blow-up case): reject when the stem asks for the strongest or exact statement. (d) The clause is a derivable upgrade (explicit formula, iff with both directions provable): prefer it over S. If no option is of type (d), answer S.
